extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A synthetic texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models and refined for high quality and diversity.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated by translating descriptive prompts into texture images using Stable Diffusion, followed by a three-stage refinement process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were generated using the Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged by the NSFW filter were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images, and flagged images were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) frequency filtering to remove object-like images, (2) patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images, and (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure alignment with prompts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluators were shown 100 images each and asked to rate the overall quality and how well the image represented the provided descriptor on a scale of 1 to 5.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mean quality and representative scores were calculated at different stages of the refinement process, showing that combining all refinement steps provided an overall 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset provides valuable resources for advancing interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The generation process exhibited bias in the safety filter, where certain texture descriptors like 'paisley' consistently triggered the NSFW filter despite lacking explicit content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The generation process struggles with creating structured textures, as simple but structured textures like grid and polka-dotted tend to have worse scores.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for texture-based research and applications, such as measuring texture bias and uncovering learned associations between objects and textures in models.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: To ensure a consistent number of images, we regenerated images flagged by the filter... for ethical reasons we exclude these flagged images from our final dataset and do not release them publicly.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: This process consists of three filtering steps, each targeting different aspects of image quality: (1) frequency filtering to remove object-like images, (2) patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images, and (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure alignment with the prompts.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Each participant was shown 100 images in random order and asked two questions for each image: (1) How would you rate the overall quality of the image? and (2) How well does the image represent the provided descriptor? Participants were asked to supply a rating on a scale of 1 to 5

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Here, we take the mean quality and representative scores, provided by our human evaluators, across the images at different stages of the refinement process... Combining all refinement steps together provides us with an overall 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: This work demonstrates that generative models, when carefully adapted, can yield extensive, versatile datasets for texture analysis, contributing valuable resources for advancing interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine leaming.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Surprisingly, texture descriptors like “paisley” consistently triggered the filter, with nearly 100% of prompts containing “paisley” producing at least one flagged image... This indicates that the high NSFW flagging rates are a broader issue with generating texture images

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Meanwhile, more simple, but more structured textures, such as grid and polka-dotted textures tend to have worse scores. This indicates that while the refinement process enhances general quality, there is room for improvement in generating more structured textures.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This multi-stage refinement process enables PTD to serve as a high-quality, representative dataset for texture-based research and applications... we highlight the usefulness of the Prompted Textures Dataset as a way to measure texture bias.
